gaps.category: RMG/export-factory sub-supplier compliance: BGMEA/BKMEA membership, utilisation declaration (UD) and Accord/Alliance/RSC-style safety and remediation files for small subcontract garment and washing units
gaps.first_search: ক্ষুদ্র গার্মেন্টস সাবকন্ট্রাক্ট কারখানা ইউডি ইউপি বন্ড লাইসেন্স নবায়ন বিজিএমইএ সদস্যপদ
gaps.why: Bangladesh has thousands of small subcontract garment, knit, washing and accessory units; UD/bond is partly covered by K01 but the small-unit buyer and its repeat audit and licence paperwork were never screened.

gaps.category: Trade licence and municipal/union parishad duties: city corporation trade licence, signboard and tax renewal, and the 2024-26 digitisation of trade licences
gaps.first_search: ট্রেড লাইসেন্স নবায়ন অনলাইন সিটি কর্পোরেশন ২০২৬ ফি সাইনবোর্ড কর
gaps.why: Every small shop and firm renews a trade licence yearly. The coverage mentions it only in passing, as 'general knowledge, unverified'. The recurring buyer group is the largest in the country and was never examined, including TIN, BIN and e-return deadlines for sole traders.

gaps.category: RJSC/Registrar of Joint Stock Companies annual returns and the Companies Act amendments; Registrar of Societies/Trade Organisations; Cooperative annual returns for small private limited firms and associations
gaps.first_search: আরজেএসসি বার্ষিক রিটার্ন দাখিল প্রাইভেট লিমিটেড কোম্পানি জরিমানা ২০২৫ নতুন নিয়ম
gaps.why: Small private limited companies and trade bodies must file annual returns and renew every year. The pass covered NGOs and co-operatives but not the RJSC annual-return duty, nor the Societies Registration and Trade Organisations Ordinance renewals.

gaps.category: Mobile financial service agents, bKash/Nagad agents, and SIM/biometric registration retailers
gaps.first_search: এমএফএস এজেন্ট কেওয়াইসি বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংক নির্দেশনা ২০২৬ সিম রেজিস্ট্রেশন বায়োমেট্রিক খুচরা বিক্রেতা জরিমানা
gaps.why: Bangladesh has over a million MFS agents and SIM/recharge retailers. Bangladesh Bank agent KYC and BTRC biometric SIM registration rules fall on these small operators, and the regime was not screened.

gaps.category: Tannery, leather and small polluting-industry operators: DoE Environmental Clearance Certificate renewal and effluent treatment (ETP) duties, outside brick kilns
gaps.first_search: পরিবেশ ছাড়পত্র নবায়ন অনলাইন ডিওই কমলা লাল শ্রেণি ক্ষুদ্র শিল্প ইটিপি বাধ্যতামূলক ২০২৫
gaps.why: DoE ECC renewal (orange and red category) falls on thousands of small mills, dyeing units, plastic recyclers, and relocated tanneries. Only brick kilns were screened, so the wider DoE clearance regime is missing.

gaps.category: Tobacco, bidi and cigarette retail / tobacco-product licensing, and the new e-commerce/F-commerce registration duty (Digital Commerce Operation Guidelines, Digital Commerce Policy)
gaps.first_search: ই-কমার্স এফ-কমার্স উদ্যোক্তা নিবন্ধন বাধ্যতামূলক ডিজিটাল কমার্স নীতিমালা ভোক্তা অধিকার অধিদপ্তর লাইসেন্স ২০২৬
gaps.why: The 2021 Digital Commerce Operation Guidelines and later Bangladesh Commerce ministry/DNCRP registration moves put duties on F-commerce and small online sellers, and the pass never checked them. Retail tobacco-licence proposals (2023 tobacco control rules) also affect millions of small shops.

candidates.buyer: Restaurants, bakeries, sweet shops, caterers, juice bars, dairy and packaged-food makers, street food sellers. About 450,000 food-sale establishments (ITV, 23 Aug 2026), and the real number is higher.
candidates.category: 20. Small licensed premises: small food producers (also 19 street vendors)
candidates.evidence: https://food.chemlinked.com/database/view/6995 ; https://bangladeshmonitor.com.bd/en/all-food-businesses-to-require-bfsa-registration-under-new-rules ; https://www.itvbd.com/national/273722/%E0%A6%96%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%BE%E0%A7%9F-%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A7%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%82%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%95-%E0%A6%B9%E0%A6%9A%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%9B%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%A6-%E0%A6%96%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF ; https://bangla.thedailystar.net/business/news-3945381 (fetch timed out; title and snippet only). Businesses today need permits from 13+ agencies and fear harassment. BFSA says enforcement starts with large industrial producers.
candidates.existing: Competitor search (Bangla, 'নিরাপদ খাদ্য লাইসেন্স রেজিস্ট্রেশন সেবা সফটওয়্যার কনসালট্যান্ট এজেন্সি') found no Bangladeshi software or consultant for this rule; results were Indian FSSAI services. A free BFSA online portal is implied but its name and cost were not found. No existing solution confirmed.
candidates.known_note: No known idea covers food premises. Not K09 (pharmacies).
candidates.name: Food business registration and renewal under Safe Food (Registration and License) Regulations 2026
candidates.trigger: S.R.O. 269-Law/2026 of the Bangladesh Safe Food Authority, issued 16 July 2026 and in force at once. Five controls: mandatory registration (Schedule 1), business licence, premises licence, production or import licence with product registration. Valid 3 years, then renewal. Process is online, with one database. Licence needed for infant food, fortified, organic and GM food, edible oil and private food warehouses.
candidates.unchecked: Fee schedule (Schedule 10) and which premises fall in which schedule; the portal name, whether it is free and easy; grace period or enforcement dates for small shops; BFSA's own website; whether done-for-you application help sells to tiny shops; overlap with trade licence and BSTI CM licence.

candidates.buyer: Owners of a few commercial vehicles; small transport companies
candidates.category: 18. Transport operators
candidates.existing: Competitor search (Bangla, 'ফ্লিট ম্যানেজমেন্ট সফটওয়্যার বাংলাদেশ ... ফিটনেস ট্যাক্স টোকেন রুট পারমিট রিমাইন্ডার') found Prism ERP fleet module (renewal alerts, aimed at larger firms), VTS Transport Management app (document renewal tracking), Bdtask VMS (about USD 3,999). BRTA portal and bKash take payments. Brokers (dalals) handle fitness for many owners.
candidates.name: Vehicle paper-renewal tracker for small bus, truck and minibus owners (fitness, tax token, route permit, licence)
candidates.trigger: Road Transport Act 2018 (s.16 registration, s.25 fitness; up to 6 months' jail or Tk 25,000). BRTA extended no-penalty renewal of fitness, tax token, route permit and driving licence to 29 Oct 2026. The High Court ruled that vehicles without renewed fitness cannot run.
candidates.unchecked: Owner count and fleet sizes; willingness to pay; whether the dalal channel or the owners' associations can be a sales route; whether VTS is cheap and widely used.

candidates.buyer: Small jewellery shops that buy old gold (BAJUS members and non-members)
candidates.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
candidates.existing: No competitor search run (budget exhausted). Rules found are trade-body guidance, not statute, so it is unclear who inspects them.
candidates.name: Old-gold purchase register and hallmark records for small jewellers
candidates.trigger: BAJUS Jewellery Buying, Selling and Marketing Guidelines 2023: receipt with seller name, address, mobile and NID; keep the NID copy; no purchase from non-owners; hallmark on ornaments; diamond memo details. Gold policy 2018 (cabinet approved). 5% VAT included in price, minimum 6% making charge (Jan 2026).
candidates.unchecked: Whether the state or police require a register; jewellery POS vendors; VAT register duties for jewellers; count of shops (BAJUS).

candidates.buyer: Small and mid-size foreign-funded NGOs and charities
candidates.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities
candidates.existing: None found; competitor search not run.
candidates.name: NGO Affairs Bureau renewal, project-approval and annual-report tracker for small foreign-funded NGOs
candidates.trigger: Foreign Donations (Voluntary Activities) Regulation Ordinance 1978 and NGOAB rules: registration renewal, project approval, reports. A circular dated 3 March (year not confirmed, possibly 2025) eased new registration and set project-approval deadlines.
candidates.unchecked: Annual report and renewal steps and deadlines; NGOAB online system (it may be a free portal); how many small NGOs; local donor-compliance consultants.

candidates.buyer: Owners of industrial boilers
candidates.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
candidates.existing: None found; no online boiler system found; no competitor search run.
candidates.name: Boiler use-certificate renewal tracker for small boiler owners (rice mills, dyeing units, laundries, small factories)
candidates.trigger: Boilers Act 2022 and Boiler Rules 2025 (replacing the 1961 Rules): use-certificate renewal on expiry, transfer, repair, 90+ days idle or accident. Chief Inspector approval for imported boilers (Bangladesh Bank notice, June 2026).
candidates.unchecked: Current boiler count (the 5,039 figure is old); renewal interval under the 2025 Rules; owner mix (many are large garment or textile firms, which are out of scope); who sells inspection help.

candidates.buyer: Feed dealers, small feed mills, fish-feed sellers
candidates.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers (also 14)
candidates.existing: None found. No competitor search run. DLS online licence status not confirmed.
candidates.name: Licence and renewal tool for animal-feed and fish-feed sellers and small feed mills
candidates.trigger: Fish Feed and Animal Feed Act 2010 and Animal Feed Rules 2013: licence for manufacture, import, sale; 1-year validity; renew 30+ days before expiry. DLS licenses animal feed; DoF licenses fish feed.
candidates.unchecked: Number of licensed sellers; whether DLS or DoF run online renewal; record-keeping or batch duties; whether the vet-medicine shop licence is separate and which authority issues it.

candidates.buyer: Retail pesticide dealers, pest-control firms (same shops as K05 fertiliser dealers)
candidates.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
candidates.existing: None found; no competitor search run.
candidates.name: Pesticide retail dealer licence and certification tracker for agro-input dealers
candidates.trigger: Pesticides Act 2018: licence for sale and pest-control services (DAE). A 2024 blog says a dealer certification and training scheme was planned (unverified).
candidates.unchecked: Whether the dealer certification rules were issued and by when; renewal cycle; stock or sales register duties; overlap with K05 dealers (one product could serve both).

candidates.buyer: Jar-water plants, small bottled-water, bakery, spice and snack makers
candidates.category: 13. Small water systems (also 20)
candidates.existing: None found; no competitor search run. BSTI has its own licensing system (unverified).
candidates.name: BSTI CM licence tracker for small jar-water and packaged-food makers
candidates.trigger: BSTI Act 2018: mandatory CM licence for listed products (jar water is on the list; one source says 299 products, another 191). Validity 3 years. Mobile courts fine unlicensed makers; the High Court ordered action on unsafe jar water.
candidates.unchecked: Current licence counts; BSTI portal; whether record-keeping for lab tests is a recurring duty; overlap with the Safe Food regulation for packaged food (see C1).

candidates.buyer: Owners of irrigation deep tube-wells, plus drillers
candidates.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
candidates.existing: None found; no competitor search run.
candidates.name: Irrigation well (deep tube-well) licence tracker for pump owners
candidates.trigger: Groundwater Management for Agricultural Purposes Act 2018: licence from the Upazila Parishad irrigation committee; unlicensed wells face a fine or jail (2017 draft: Tk 10,000 or 7 days).
candidates.unchecked: Whether the Act is enforced and the 2023 rules exist (not found); renewal cycle; buyers are farmers with low willingness to pay.

candidates.buyer: Haat lessees (ijaradars) of city-corporation cattle markets
candidates.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
candidates.existing: Private online cattle platforms exist (Bikroy, Daraz, Bengalmeat and others) but not lessee tools.

candidates.trigger: City corporations lease Eid cattle haats (27 for Dhaka North and South in the season reported). Government 'digital haat' was dropped for private platforms.
candidates.unchecked: Whether lessees file any report; seasonal and single-event use; lessees tend to be politically connected larger operators.

candidates.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
candidates.existing: None found; no competitor search run.

candidates.trigger: Bangladesh Bank FEPD: renewal needs minimum annual FX turnover (USD 500k in Dhaka and Chattogram, USD 350k elsewhere per 2021-22 circulars); fee via BEFTN under the 12 Jan 2025 circular; returns through authorised dealer banks; limit on cash held at office.

candidates.buyer: Urban households employing domestic workers (about 2.5 million workers)
candidates.category: 1. Household employers
candidates.existing: None found.
candidates.name: Household employers of domestic workers (Labour Act 2026 partial coverage)
candidates.trigger: Labour (Amendment) Act 2026 extends accident compensation and union rights to domestic workers (single HR-vendor blog). No registration or filing duty found.
candidates.unchecked: Official gazette text of the 2026 Act on domestic workers; any registration or contract duty in its rules; households unlikely to pay.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: No registration duty on households found. Domestic Workers Protection and Welfare Policy 2015 is non-binding and poorly enforced (about 2.5 million workers per social welfare adviser). Labour (Amendment) Act 2026 (in force 10 April 2026) gives domestic workers only partial cover (accident compensation, union rights), per one HR-vendor blog (unverified). Nothing a household must file.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No licensing regime for scrap or old-iron dealers found (city-corporation trade licence only, general knowledge, unverified). Ship-breaking yards and their DASR bottleneck under the Hong Kong Convention are already K06.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Nothing found on a second-hand dealer or pawnbroker register in Bangladesh. Closest item is the BAJUS rule on buying old gold (see 4).

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: BAJUS Jewellery Buying, Selling and Marketing Guidelines 2023 require a receipt with seller name, address, mobile and NID, a retained NID copy for old gold, and hallmarking. This is a trade-body rule, not statute. Gold policy 2018 exists. No BSTI hallmark mandate for 2026 found. 5% VAT is included in the price (Jan 2026 report). One candidate logged (C3).

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler or used-parts licence found in Bangladesh. Only generic trade licence and VAT apply (unverified).

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: City corporations lease seasonal cattle haats (27 in Dhaka North and South for Eid). The government 'digital haat' was dropped and online sales are now private. No trader register found. Weak lessee-toll idea logged (C10).

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: No Bangladesh licensing detail found. Opinion piece says modern slaughterhouses are lacking. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No search spent (budget). Expected to be tiny and unregulated.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Bangladesh Veterinary Council Act 2019 registers practitioners. Fish Feed and Animal Feed Act 2010 and Animal Feed Rules 2013 need an annual licence for feed makers, importers and sellers, renewed at least 30 days before expiry. No licence process found for vet-medicine shops. Feed seller idea logged (C6).

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Groundwater Management for Agricultural Purposes Act 2018: licence for irrigation wells via the Upazila Parishad irrigation committee. A 2017 draft penalty was Tk 10,000 or 7 days' jail. No driller licence found. Logged as unverified (C9).

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Only the 2017 Institutional and Regulatory Framework for Faecal Sludge Management (guideline). No operator licensing found for 2024-2025. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Boilers Act 2022 (Act 6) replaced the 1923 Act; Boiler Rules 2025 replaced the 1961 Rules. Use-certificate renewal is triggered by expiry, transfer, repair, 90+ days idle or an accident. About 5,039 boilers and 8 inspectors (older figures). A June 2026 Bangladesh Bank notice needs Chief Inspector approval to import boilers. No online boiler system found. Lifts: no regulator or law; BSTI says it lacks authority (Financial Express, TBS). Boiler idea logged (C5).

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Jar and bottled water is under mandatory BSTI CM licensing (32 parameters). A 2014 estimate put about 1,200 jar-water sellers against about 160 licensed, and many run only on a city trade licence. No private-supplier licence under WASA found. Logged (C8).

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Pesticides Act 2018 requires a licence for import, sale and pest-control services, issued by DAE. A 2024 blog says a certification, registration and mandatory training scheme for retail agro-input dealers was in preparation (unverified). Fertiliser dealers are K05. Logged (C7).

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Overseas recruiters are K15 (rejected). Ministry cancelled 49 agency licences under the 2013 Act (section 13) and the High Court upheld it. No labour-supply or outsourcing registry found.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Nothing on cemetery, hearse or burial-society licensing in Bangladesh. Death registration runs through the state BDRIS portal and ward offices. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: NGO Affairs Bureau: registration, renewal and project approval for foreign-funded NGOs; an NGOAB circular (3 March, year unclear) eased registration and set project-approval deadlines. Annual report details not confirmed. Halal certification was not searched. NGO idea logged (C4) as unverified.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Road Transport Act 2018 requires fitness, tax token and route permit. BRTA extended the no-penalty renewal window to 29 Oct 2026 (the BRTA portal and bKash handle payment). Competitors seen: Prism ERP fleet module, VTS Transport Management app, Bdtask VMS. Logged (C2).

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money changers: Bangladesh Bank licence renewal needs a minimum annual FX turnover (USD 500k in Dhaka and Chattogram, USD 350k elsewhere per 2021-22 circulars), fee paid by BEFTN under the 12 Jan 2025 circular, and returns via authorised dealer banks. Number of licensees is small. DSCC plans mandatory licences for private market operators (headline only). Street vendors are now inside the food registration rule (C1). Logged (C11, C12).

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Strongest finding: Safe Food (Registration and License) Regulations 2026, in force 16 July 2026 (see C1). BSTI CM licences also apply to small food makers (3-year validity). BRTA driving-school licence form exists; no fee or rule details. No childcare or day-care regime found. Tattoo and hunting: not applicable.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Searched BERC/LPG. Found only price-cap enforcement (BERC raised 12kg LPG to Tk1,837 for Oct 2026; retailers charge Tk2,200-2,700; Khulna admin ordered price lists displayed; BERC told bottlers to issue VAT invoices/delivery orders). No filing, register or QR/cylinder-tracking duty found. Petrol-pump explosives licence renewal and dealer reporting not found (search returned nothing). Weak candidate listed.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: No dedicated search (budget spent on other categories). Rice mills/grain traders are already K04; nothing new beyond K04. Cold storage and warehouse licences unchecked.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Co-operative Dept annual audit then AGM resolution within 1 month is a documented duty (district co-op office PDFs, garbled text). About 697-756 licensed NGO-MFIs under MRA Act 2006 report twice a year (data) and yearly (financials); a Microfinance Bank Ordinance 2025 is proposed (Jan 2026 report, status unconfirmed). Co-op online audit/return portal not confirmed. MFI MIS market likely crowded (unchecked).

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: DGHS hospital/clinic/diagnostic licences renew online (Prothom Alo: 11,773 renewal applications online, 4,516 renewed); Jugantor reports a new rule from FY2026-27 (details unreadable, page returned 403); DGHS raids on unlicensed clinics. No insurer-billing mandate found. A free DGHS portal exists, which limits the gap.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Pharmacy: nothing new beyond K09. DNC licenses import, transport, manufacture, sale, storage and use of precursors under the Narcotics Control Act 2018; I found no renewal process, fee or portal details. Unverified.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private security agencies are licensed by the Home Ministry (2006-era regime: Tk2 lakh fee, Tk5 lakh deposit, renewal every 2 years at Tk50,000, guard training, uniform approval; Dhaka Tribune 2017: about 700 firms ran on trade licences only). A bdlaws Act page exists (act-print-935). Current rules unverified. Overseas recruiters: K15. The July 2026 cancellation of 49 recruiting-agency licences was upheld in Oct 2026, so no new product from it.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers
coverage.found: e-GP is mandatory for public procurement. BPPA revised registration and renewal fees in Aug 2025. A new PPR 2025 is being drafted. Contractor registration/tender services are likely crowded. No site-register or local-content duty found. Quarry/sand leases not reached.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: REDMA 2010 s.5 requires developer registration plus REHAB membership (MoC notification 2017). Developers are AML-covered (CDD, 5-year records, STRs to BFIU under the Money Laundering Prevention Rules 2019, per a secondary source). The Registration (Amendment) Ordinance 2026 (early Jan 2026) allows e-registration via government-approved software (s.77A) and extends the deed registration window from 30 to 60 days. Rules and portal not yet confirmed.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals
coverage.found: Residential hotels must give guest lists to the local police station (DMP statement, 2020; poorly followed). No 2025-26 rule, e-register or tourism levy found. Special Branch launched an E-Arrival/E-Departure card portal for foreign air travellers (Aug 2026 report, single source), which is not a hotel duty.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules
coverage.found: Bangladesh Bank FEPD-1 Circular 26 (30 Jul 2026, valid 1 year) pushes electronic EXP forms via OEMS and exempts marketplace e-commerce exports up to US$1,000 from the EXP form. ERC is renewed yearly via CCI&E. EPB registration now lasts 5 years (CoO/GSP/REX need valid registration). BSW makes CLP document submission mandatory (single source, unverified). Hilsa export permits are case by case. Shrimp: K10. Customs/BSW tools: K01/K03. Nothing new that is strong.

coverage.category: 31. Brick kilns (Brick Manufacturing and Kilns Establishment (Control) Act 2013 as amended; DoE clearance)
coverage.found: About 7,881 kilns (June 2022): 3,248 legal, 4,633 without clearance. The Sep 2024 adviser said no new clearances and that 3,491 kilns without clearance would be closed. Amendment to the Act under discussion. Enforcement is by fines and mobile courts. Low software gap and a shrinking base.

coverage.category: 32. Animal feed, fish feed and hatchery licensing (Feed Act 2010, Animal Feed Rules 2013, Fish Feed Rules 2011)
coverage.found: Feed licences run one year, with DLS for animal feed and DoF for fish feed. Renewal appears to be in person (wikiprocedure, undated). No online portal confirmed. Small base and unclear reporting duty.

coverage.category: 33. Internet service providers and BTRC licensing (ISP Guideline 2020, 2025 licensing reform)
coverage.found: ISP licences renew every 5 years and tariffs need approval. Cl.25.4 requires user-history and traffic logs kept for at least 3 months. BTRC cancelled 16 ISP licences for non-renewal (Nov 2025) and earlier 334 for failing to renew. The 2025 reform migrates ISPs to FTSP/District FTSP licences (draft sent for approval 24 May 2026; 5.5% revenue share proposal opposed by ISPAB). Many small local ISPs exist. Competitors found: Codonyx Net Manager and RapidLogX (IP log/BTRC compliance), BD-ISP.

coverage.category: 34. Hajj and Umrah agencies (Hajj and Umrah Management; Ministry of Religious Affairs)
coverage.found: 1,275 licensed agencies (941 eligible for Hajj, 753 registered pilgrims, 70 lead agencies; undated). 2026 conditions: written contracts with pilgrims for Makkah/Madinah services, and penalties for agencies that do not register pilgrims. 2027 pre-registration opened 27 Jul 2026 at Tk3.5 lakh (unclear source date). Only generic Umrah software (PHPTravels) found. A government Hajj system is likely and unchecked.

coverage.category: 35. Fire licences (Fire Service and Civil Defence e-Fire licence)
coverage.found: FSCD launched an e-fire licence system on 30 Apr 2026. From 1 May 2026, new licences, renewals and re-evaluations are online only and manual applications are closed. Builder is Perky Rabbit Corporation Ltd (Financial Express). Who needs the licence, renewal period and fees not confirmed. A free state portal limits the opportunity to a done-for-you service.

coverage.category: 36. BSTI mandatory certification (CM licence) for small manufacturers, importers and packers
coverage.found: 273 products were under mandatory CM in Jun 2024, fewer than half food. Items added include fruit drinks, wafers, 36 new items including sweets, and 43 items. BSTI Act 2018 makes marketing without a CM licence an offence. Renewal lapses are common (47 edible-oil refineries). Overlaps category 20 (small food producers), which another worker covers. 2026 list and fees not found.

coverage.category: 37. Deed writers and sub-registry e-registration (Registration Act 1908 as amended by the Ordinance 2026)
coverage.found: Ordinance of early Jan 2026 added s.77A (e-registration through government-approved software). The rules and portal date are not found. The state builds the system (out of scope). Possible intermediary tools for deed writers/lawyers once rules exist.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No beekeeper-specific licence or mandatory register found. Only the generic BSTI CM licence for packaged honey (reported fee Tk 1,000 first issue, Tk 500 renewal, via BSTI app/e-services; Prothom Alo, unverified current). DAE has proposed a national beekeeper database, with about 3,500 beekeepers estimated by 2025-26 per an opinion piece (unverified). The Sundarbans honey GI registration is not a recurring duty. Tiny and unregulated; no candidate.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses (cold storage / warehouse licence gap)
coverage.found: Cold storage: the only 2026 rule found is the Agricultural Marketing Directorate's cap on potato cold-storage rent (Tk 6/kg to 31 Dec, notice of 31 Aug), with owners demanding Tk 7. No cold-storage licence renewal rule or register was found in the results. Owners are already organised in an association. Weak lead; K04 still covers rice mills and grain traders. Warehouse licence not verified.

coverage.category: RMG/export-factory sub-supplier compliance: BGMEA/BKMEA membership, UD and safety/remediation files for small subcontract garment and washing units
coverage.found: The searches found no document-level rule specific to small subcontract units. What exists: BGMEA/BKMEA issue e-UDs (NBR ASYCUDA World integrated with BGMEA e-UD; unit-price declaration required in UD applications), the 2019 Commerce Ministry RMG subcontracting guidelines make subcontract factories register with the associations (older, details may be outdated), and BGMEA suspended UD issuance to 84 non-compliant units in Jan 2020 after a DIFE letter. BGMEA's FY2026-27 budget ask (UD items without repeated bond-licence amendments) is a proposal only. No small-unit software buyer confirmed.

coverage.category: Trade licence and municipal/union parishad duties: city corporation trade licence, signboard and tax renewal, and 2024-26 digitisation
coverage.found: Trade licences are renewed yearly (reported deadline 30 June; late fee applies) through city corporation, pourashava or union parishad portals. DNCC and DSCC accept online payment, with a 10% rebate for paying the four instalments at once (DNCC extension to 30 Nov for FY2024-25). DSCC announced a plan for 5-year renewal, and the portal etradelicense.gov.bd exists. BSS reports that banks and city corporations will integrate with the BIDA OSS platform for online licences. Two opinion pieces propose automatic renewal reminders. The 2026 fee table and signboard-tax rates were not found. Free state portals cover most of the duty, so only a reminder or compliance-calendar layer remains.

coverage.category: RJSC annual returns and Companies Act amendments; Registrar of Societies / trade organisations; cooperative returns for small private limited firms and associations
coverage.found: The annual return is mandatory under the Companies Act 1994, though sources conflict on the deadline (28 days vs 21 days after the AGM; the first return within 18 months of incorporation). Reported penalty is a daily fine of about Tk 200 up to a cap, plus the risk of being struck off (secondary law-firm sources only, unverified). A draft Companies (Third Amendment) Act 2026 was at consultation in Sept 2026 (BSS, 7 Sept 2026): digital registration, beneficial-ownership disclosure and Registrar fines up to Tk 50,000 are reported. Not enacted. An RJSC online portal accepts annual returns. Societies Registration / Trade Organisations Ordinance renewals were not reached by these searches.

coverage.category: Mobile financial service agents, bKash/Nagad agents, and SIM/biometric registration retailers
coverage.found: Bangladesh Bank BRPD circular 08 of 11 Mar 2026 updates the e-KYC guideline (BFIU Circular 25 of 2020) for banks, MFS and PSPs; the insurance and capital-market circular sets a 31 Dec 2026 implementation date, and the MFS date is unverified. The duty sits on the MFS provider and operators, not on the agents, who work in the operators' own agent apps. BTRC: a 10-SIM-per-NID cap and a Central Biometric Verification Monitoring Platform, plus handset registration (NEIR) blocking of unregistered phones from Dec 2025 (Oct 2025 report). Prothom Alo reports retailers stealing fingerprints at SIM sale. No retailer-level fine or register rule found. Operator-controlled and low willingness to pay; no candidate.

coverage.category: Tannery, leather and small polluting-industry operators: DoE ECC renewal and ETP duties, outside brick kilns
coverage.found: The ECR (Environment Conservation Rules 2023) classify industry as Green, Orange-A, Orange-B and Red. Sources conflict on renewal: one says 1 year for Orange and Red and 3 years for Green, another says yearly. The DoE has online ECC application with SMS/email status (2019 project description). The DoE gave a final warning to 2,046 factories in Dhaka, Gazipur, Narayanganj and Narsingdi to keep ETPs running (TBS). A 2026 BSS item says ETPs will be brought under online monitoring (Buriganga; planned). Renewal needs compliance monitoring reports. A per-factory ECC/ETP compliance-file and renewal tracker candidate was found.

coverage.category: Tobacco, bidi and cigarette retail licensing, and the e-commerce/F-commerce registration duty (Digital Commerce Operation Guidelines / Policy)
coverage.found: E-commerce: the Digital Commerce Operation Guidelines 2021 and DBID Registration Guidelines 2022 already require DBID (applied through RJSC; can be had without a trade licence if a website/page exists; terms must be in Bangla). Uptake was low: 393 DBIDs in five months, 1,902 by 2023. A Digital Commerce Authority ordinance draft (Prothom Alo, 29 Aug 2025; earlier 2023 draft) would require a licence; it is not law, and the cabinet approved a similar draft in May 2024 before it stalled. A Cross-Border Digital Commerce Policy 2026 draft (published 22 July, comments to 6 Aug) targets foreign platforms and vendors. Tobacco: a 2022 proposal would require a separate one-year renewable licence for retail sale of cigarettes, bidi and jarda; the amendment was still in consultation in Dec 2025 and no final law was confirmed. Both unenacted.
